question: Does continuous capture body condition improve project-held-out ranking of migration activation above ordinal Durif stage, length and release timing?
source: the same six-project expert-corrected public eel meta-analysis panel used in the V4 manuscript
folds: leave one entire project out; fit both models on the remaining projects; evaluate only score rankings within the held-out project's release-year strata
cohort: all source-evaluable exact FIII/FIV/FV eels with stage, release, length, weight and source migration classification; preserve nine 2015 expert non-migrant corrections
base_model: project-year intercepts + centered body length per 100 mm + centered release timing per 100 days + ordinal Durif stage
expanded_model: same base model + standardized capture allometric weight-for-length residual (adjusted for project and capture Durif)
primary_metric: pair-weighted within-project-year AUC/concordance difference (expanded minus base), computed from initiator/non-initiator pairs without using held-out outcomes for coefficient estimation
confidence: 500 seed-20261008 stratified fish-label bootstrap replicates within each held-out project-year to assess conditional evaluation variability; training weights are held fixed, so not a full model-development CI
secondary: individual held-out project deltas, including projects with no evaluable mixed-outcome stratum
stage-only versus stage-plus-condition contrast without the length/timing controls as ecological descriptive benchmark
support_rule: An incremental held-out body-condition ranking gain requires positive primary AUC difference with a conditional-bootstrap 95% CI above zero; project-level consistency must be reported, not hidden. Results are developmental even if supported.
boundaries: AUC is a ranking metric only; no held-out-project calibration intercept is estimated, so no claim of calibrated absolute migration probabilities.
Held-out predictor pre-processing uses project/stage morphometrics without outcomes; only regression coefficients are cross-fitted.
The condition residual uses body weight and length which also contribute to Durif classification; no independent energetic mechanism is inferred.
A bootstrap on held-out observations with fixed training weights excludes uncertainty in training and is not a full independent-project replication.
If expanded score does not beat the base model, the earlier positive within-panel condition coefficient must not be promoted as demonstrated out-of-project added utility.
